disputed: Velchik declined to comment to the Boston Globe on the essay and emails when they were reported in Sept. 2025. The Latin paper was an assigned exercise to write from the perspective of 'a controversial historical or literary figure' — students could choose the figure, and choosing Hitler specifically is what unnerved the instructor enough to require a redo. His later emails calling Mein Kampf his favorite book of the year and praising Hitler's oratory/propaganda skills did not mention the Holocaust, which critics have highlighted as notable; whether this reflects genuine sympathy versus edgy intellectual provocation is a matter of interpretation, not established fact.

items: As a Harvard senior in 2011, Michael Velchik submitted a Latin-class paper written from the perspective of Adolf Hitler, for an assignment asking students to write as a controversial historical or literary figure justifying their actions. His choice of Hitler unnerved the instructor enough that Velchik was asked to redo the assignment.

In a June 2013 email to a peer, while preparing for Harvard Law School, Velchik wrote: '[I]s it bad that my favorite class at harvard was nietzsche and my favorite book i've read this year is mein kampf?' He did not mention the Holocaust.
In a later email, Velchik wrote a brief review calling Mein Kampf 'fascinating' and remarking that Hitler 'excelled as an orator' and 'understands the importance of propaganda.'
Velchik delivered the Latin Oration at Harvard's 2012 commencement. He holds both an undergraduate and law degree from Harvard.
Reported by the Boston Globe on Sept. 2, 2025, based on accounts from three people who studied with him and a copy of the emails.
sections.label: Harvard Latin paper and Mein Kampf emails (2011–2013, reported Sept. 2025)

items: Velchik joined DOJ as senior counsel in 2025. In May 2025 he defended the administration's invocation of the Alien Enemies Act against migrants.

He was the sole lawyer arguing the government's case against Harvard University in federal court in July 2025, over the administration's cancellation of federal research funding on grounds that Harvard exhibited 'wanton indifference to antisemitism.' His Hitler-essay history surfaced in the press the following month, creating a notable contrast with the antisemitism rationale he was arguing.
sections.label: DOJ role: Harvard funding case (2025)

items: In the Sept. 2026 DOJ filing opposing CNN/MS NOW/Politico's lawsuit over their White House ban, Velchik wrote the line 'access to the White House is a privilege — not a right,' arguing for a broad expansion of presidential authority to determine which outlets can cover the White House and urging the court to overturn the precedent protecting journalist access. See related item on the press freedom rollback.
sections.label: DOJ role: CNN/MS NOW/Politico press ban defense (Sept. 2026)

summary: Michael Velchik, DOJ senior counsel, wrote a college paper from Hitler's perspective and later privately praised Mein Kampf and Hitler's oratory without mentioning the Holocaust; he has gone on to become a lead DOJ litigator defending the administration's most aggressive actions against institutions and the press — arguing Harvard showed 'wanton indifference to antisemitism' in the funding-cuts case, and in Sept. 2026 authoring the brief defending Trump's ban of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House.
title: DOJ senior counsel Michael Velchik — Hitler essay/Mein Kampf praise, Harvard case, press ban brief
